newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia announces new round of interrogations.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia announces new round of interrogations.

text.p: Indonesia announced on Thursday a fresh round of interrogations over the July riots in Jakarta, and said authorities would again question opposition figurehead Megawati Sukarnoputri.
The official Antara news agency said the former editor of the banned Tempo magazine, a former governor of Jakarta and a Catholic priest would also be questioned.
Antara quoted Pontas Pasaribu, a spokesman in the Attorney-General's office, as saying Megawati had been summoned to appear for questioning on Tuesday about the July 27 riots.

Megawati, the daughter of late founding president Sukarno, was questioned by police twice last month over the riots, which were the worst in the country's capital in two decades. The official Human Rights Commission said five people died, 149 were injured and 74 were missing.

Pasaribu said former Jakarta governor Ali Sadikin, the head of the Petition of 50 dissident group, former Tempo editor Gunawan Mohamand and Catholic priest Ismartono, a Bishop's Conference of Indonesia official, had been called for questioning on Monday.

Sadikin, Gunawan and Ismartono have been called as witnesses in the subversion case against independent labour leader Muchtar Pakpahan and Budiman Sudjatmiko, leader of the leftist People's Democratic Party (PRD).
Antara said Surjadi, the government-backed leader of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), would also be questioned on Wednesday.

The riots started after police seized the PDI headquarters from loyalist supporters of Megawati, who had taken over the building after she was replaced by Surjadi as party leader at a government-backed congress in June.
The government has blamed the PRD for instigating the riots and in recent weeks called in a number of government critics for questioning over their links with Pakpahan and the PRD.
Earlier on Thursday, a lawsuit filed by Megawati against the government over her ouster as party leader was adjourned for three weeks after a brief hearing.

The case was heard amid tight security as hundreds of troops and riot police surrounded the Central Jakarta State Court. Some 100 supporters of Megawati gathered outside, but the morning passed off peacefully.
Lawyers for Megawati asked for an injunction to prevent the rival government-backed PDI faction from occupying party headquarters.
"We have asked for the status quo to be kept while the court case is in progress," Bambang Widjojanto, one of Megawati's lawyers, told Reuters after the hearing.
"The status quo means that Megawati remains as leader of the PDI and the PDI headquarters can be occupied (only by her). We want this decision or an injunction to be made first," he said.
Chief judge I Gde Ketut Sukarata adjourned the hearing until September 26 without making a decision.
